purpose: First end-to-end symbolic reconstruction chain joining Kircher's worked Pinax-IV/Tone-II pitch example to one visually read Pinax-IV Notae Temporis series without inventing octave placement or modern tempo.

sources.primary_text: Musurgia universalis, Tomus II, Book VIII, Proposition II, pp.51-52; UNC/Internet Archive OCR around lines 67345-67464
sources.pinax_image: Musurgia universalis, Tomus II, Syntagma I Pinax IV, p.83; historical image reproduced in Cashner 2024 Figure 2; independent e-rara scan [92] still required for verification

shared_rhythm.note: The ratios are suitable for symbolic playback/visualization. No modern BPM or quarter-note mapping is claimed.

tenor.degree_status: the final 5,5 are reconstructed from Kircher's directly stated D,D output because the numeric OCR is damaged

inflection_policy.B: The Tone-II mollis system implies B-flat where the signature governs; source-letter B is preserved separately from that modern pitch-class interpretation.
inflection_policy.F: Source-letter F is preserved without automatically choosing F-natural versus contextual F-sharp. Kircher's broader example/practice can sharpen degree 7 as a leading tone, but the exact accidental placement for this phrase requires visual inspection of the notated worked example.

explicitly_not_claimed: canonical verification of the rhythm row
canonical verification against the independent e-rara p.83 witness
next_promotion_gate: Directly inspect ETH/e-rara scan [92] for Pinax-IV Vperm and rhythm glyphs and the relevant Tone-II/phonotactic source surfaces; then promote only independently agreeing data.
